synopsis: Chapter 9 and the glossary agree that only a frozen stratified random sample can support a release rate claim [f6648, f6867, f14095]. The proposed campaign implements this through a scenario-catalog-fed estimation stream using a frozen, pre-registered stratified random sample [f7355]. Simple or stratified random sampling is recommended for estimating detection, false-alarm and nuisance-brake rates because it can yield unbiased or known-weight estimates with classical confidence intervals for the declared distribution, backed by established statistics [f7239, f7240, f7246]. However, the operational distribution may be uncertain, and sampling cannot establish validity if the declared distribution is wrong [f7244, f7241]. Rare events require enormous exposure, so these methods cannot legitimately claim efficient discovery of very rare failures; no particular tooling is prescribed [f7243, f7242, f7245].
